chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad al-Kulayni narrated from Salih ibn Abi Hammad from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Nawfali from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar from some of his companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Condemned is one who engages in sexual intercourse with an animal.'

key_terms.بَهِيمَةً: An animal (beast), specifically referring to non-human animals in this context.
key_terms.مَلْعُونٌ: Condemned or cursed, indicating a state of divine displeasure or exclusion from mercy.
key_terms.نَكَحَ: To marry or engage in sexual intercourse with.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on sexual intercourse with animals?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi establishes the ruling of divine condemnation (mal'un) for bestiality, a ruling rooted in the broader Islamic prohibition of sexual acts outside the prescribed marital bond. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a primary textual evidence for the invalidity and moral corruption of copulating with animals, often discussed alongside the concept of *zawj al-bahim* in legal manuals. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Kufan scholarly tradition in preserving this specific legal maxim.

en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Muhammad al-Kulayniy has narrated from Salih ibn abu Hammad from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Nawfaliy from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Condemned is one who engages in sexual intercourse with animals.’”
